A literary heteronym is a fully developed fictional character created by an author to write under a distinct identity, complete with a unique biography, physical appearance, philosophy, and writing style. Difference from Pseudonyms

* Pseudonyms (Pen Names): Simply a false name used by an author who continues to write as themselves.
* Heteronyms: Independent personae operating outside the author's own personality, sometimes even critiquing or translating each other's work. The creator writing as themselves is referred to as the "orthonym".    * Alberto Caeiro: A pastoral, anti-philosophical poet considered the "master" of the other figures.
   * Ricardo Reis: A neoclassical poet with a formal, pagan worldview.
   * Álvaro de Campos: An exuberant, modernist engineer and futurist poet.
